articleMarkdown:
# Studying Fellowship: taking a shared purpose beyond a small circle

To accomplish something together, first make the shared purpose clear and leave room for people from different backgrounds to participate.

Several people agreeing with an idea does not necessarily make them collaborators. Fellowship describes connection at different scales, from a doorway and a clan to the outskirts and open country; it also describes defensiveness and rivalry. It asks who is included in “we,” and what brings us together. The contemporary applications in this article concern open collaboration; the warfare in the ancient text is explained as historical imagery.

## Identifying the hexagram

Tóng Rén is hexagram 13 in the traditional King Wen sequence, with the symbol ䷌. Its lower trigram is Li ☲ and its upper trigram is Qian ☰; their traditional images are fire and heaven, respectively. Count the lines from the bottom: 初九, 六二, 九三, 九四, 九五, 上九. A solid line is yang and a broken line is yin. Nine and six in the line headings identify yang and yin; they do not indicate additional lines.

The six lines are numbered from the bottom upward; the figure below displays their actual positions from top to bottom.

```text
━━━━━━  上九
━━━━━━  九五
━━━━━━  九四
━━━━━━  九三
━━  ━━  六二
━━━━━━  初九
```

## Hexagram statement

> 同人于野，亨。利涉大川，利君子貞。

Editorial rendering: Fellowship in the open country: things can go well. It is favorable to cross the great river and for an exemplary person to remain rightly steadfast.

Legge reads Fellowship as the union of people, emphasizing the wider setting of “in the open country” and arguing that such connection should extend beyond private preferences. Crossing the great river retains the image of facing major difficulties together, while beneficial constancy places a condition of right conduct on that union.

A beginner might first ask whether what we share is a specific purpose or simply a feeling of familiarity. A shared purpose cannot erase differences, and greater numbers do not automatically make it right. Participants need to understand why the undertaking deserves their involvement.

[zhouyi-13; legge1882-13]

## Interpretation in the Ten Wings

The Commentary on the Judgment (Tuan zhuan) and the Commentary on the Images (Xiang zhuan) belong to the Yi zhuan, the commentaries commonly called the Ten Wings. Their interpretations are kept separate below from the hexagram and line statements, followed by applications for contemporary learning.

The Commentary on the Judgment speaks of connecting the aspirations of all under heaven. The Commentary on the Images takes heaven and fire as its images and adds “类族辨物”: grouping by kind and distinguishing things. Commonality and discernment thus appear together; Fellowship does not require everything to be indistinguishable.

Contemporary collaboration can state a common aim while recognizing different abilities, viewpoints, and responsibilities. Treating every disagreement as disunity can make real problems harder to notice.

[zhouyi-13; hon-sep]

## Six lines, from bottom to top

The quotations below are line statements; the explanations that follow are original learning commentary. Good fortune, no blame, and regret belong to ancient divinatory language and cannot be turned directly into guarantees about an individual’s future.

### 初九 · First step beyond your own doorway

> 同人于門，無咎。

Editorial rendering: Fellowship at the doorway: no blame.

The doorway is a starting point for contact with the outside world. Legge reads it as union beginning before narrow self-interest has entered it.

When starting a shared activity, explain what you want to do in language others can understand. Do not assume newcomers already know the unspoken understandings you share with old friends.

[zhouyi-13; legge1882-13]

### 六二 · Familiar relationships can also narrow your view

> 同人于宗，吝。

Editorial rendering: Fellowship only within the clan: cause for regret.

The clan places connection within kinship. Legge uses this to discuss the limits of a union favoring those close to us; he does not describe family affection itself as wrong.

If important decisions are made only in private chats among a few acquaintances, check whether other participants can learn about them and respond. Closeness has a place, but it cannot replace an explanation of shared affairs.

[zhouyi-13; legge1882-13]

### 九三 · Defensiveness and rivalry can prevent a meeting

> 伏戎于莽，升其高陵，三歲不興。

Editorial rendering: Troops lie hidden in the undergrowth; one climbs the high ridge. For three years no campaign is launched.

Troops concealed in undergrowth, climbing high ground to watch, and prolonged inaction form an unmistakably military scene. Legge explains the standoff through the lines’ competing attempts to form a union.

In ordinary collaboration, check whether you are spending all your energy guessing others’ intentions rather than clarifying needs directly. The three years are not a countdown for a real-life conflict, and this passage supplies no tactics for covert confrontation.

[zhouyi-13; legge1882-13]

### 九四 · Stopping an attack can change the direction

> 乘其墉，弗克攻，吉。

Editorial rendering: One climbs the wall but cannot carry through the attack. Good fortune.

Someone climbs the city wall but does not continue the attack. Legge retains the pairing of stopping an attack with good fortune, allowing restraint to appear when opposing forces have already approached conflict.

If you notice that you are about to send a message solely to hurt someone, pause and rewrite it in terms of facts and requests. Actual harm still needs to be addressed; restraint does not mean giving up self-protection.

[zhouyi-13; legge1882-13]

### 九五 · The turn toward reunion cannot be separated from its cost

> 同人，先號啕而後笑。大師克相遇。

Editorial rendering: In fellowship, first loud weeping, then laughter. A great army overcomes the obstacle, and they meet.

The text moves from loud weeping to laughter, then describes a great army overcoming obstacles so that a meeting becomes possible. This is no gentle story without conflict; Legge likewise reads it as union achieved after obstruction.

A contemporary analogy might be two parties finally clearing up a misunderstanding and finding a workable goal again. This does not mean every conflict ends in reunion, and ancient warfare must not become a reason to compel people to collaborate.

[zhouyi-13; legge1882-13]

### 上九 · A limited connection can still be valid

> 同人于郊，無悔。

Editorial rendering: Fellowship in the outskirts: no remorse.

Union reaches the outskirts, yet the Commentary on the Images still says the aspiration is unfulfilled. Legge notes that its reach is not yet universal, but that need not cause regret.

Some collaborations work only within a particular project and need not become relationships in which everything is shared. Recognizing their limits can make clarity and mutual respect easier to sustain.

[zhouyi-13; legge1882-13]

## A neighborhood map that includes more than familiar viewpoints

Original contemporary scenario

The following contemporary scenario was created for learning.

A few longtime friends want to map public spaces in their neighborhood. Their first list includes only places they often visit. Someone suggests inviting newer residents and neighbors with different ways of getting around to contribute, and explaining whom the map is meant to help and what problems it should address.

Different views emerge in discussion: some people value lively places, while others need quiet. The organizers do not ask everyone to share the same preferences. Instead, they clearly mark the different needs and identify which information has been verified.

The map may not satisfy everyone, but its participants and practical uses are now clearer. Fellowship’s value for contemporary learning lies in making room for differences within a shared purpose, rather than creating a small circle that always agrees.

## Common misreadings

1. Fellowship does not promise that everyone will get along. Defensiveness, stopping an attack, and limited union all appear in its six lines; solidarity alone is only part of the picture.

2. A hexagram cannot identify enemies or predict betrayal. Nor can it justify excluding a category of people or forcing others to join.

## Three practices

1. State the shared purpose in one sentence and check whether a newcomer can understand it.

2. Identify a person or role currently lacking a voice whose interests will nevertheless be affected by the outcome.

3. Separate matters that require agreement from those where differences can remain.

## Related reading

### Holding Together (hexagram-08)

Holding Together emphasizes the foundations of closeness and trust. Fellowship takes the inquiry further into the scope of union and its public purpose. A close relationship and sharing responsibility for an undertaking can support each other, but they are not the same thing.

## Closing question

When reading Fellowship, ask: does my “we” leave room for the people who are actually concerned?

## Textual note

For the fourth nine, this article uses the variant 墉 explicitly listed in the Chinese source; the main text on that page has 庸. It retains the form 無 used in the edition on which this hexagram is based.
